source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — Time complexity — dict 'x in d' is O(1) average

exercises.question: The lesson's `two_sum` makes one pass with a dict called `seen`. Select every statement that is true of that approach.
options: `seen` maps each value it has passed to that value's index
for each number it looks up `target - number` before storing it
the returned pair is ordered as the earlier index then the later one
it sorts the numbers before searching
it compares every pair of numbers with two nested loops
correct_answer: `seen` maps each value it has passed to that value's index
for each number it looks up `target - number` before storing it
the returned pair is ordered as the earlier index then the later one
exercises.explanation: One pass, keyed by complement lookup: `seen[need]` is necessarily an earlier index than the current `i`. Sorting or nested loops are the slower approaches this lesson replaces.

lessons.title: 5. Unit 5 Checkpoint: Hash Maps
lessons.description: Implement `intersection(a, b)` returning sorted unique common elements.
lessons.solution_code:
def intersection(a, b):
    return sorted(set(a) & set(b))
